prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which bifunctional PROTAC molecules and molecular glues recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to eliminate chosen proteins

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B066 for Crews, Deshaies and Handa. Targeted protein degradation turned regulated proteolysis into a defined chemical design principle, induced proximity between an E3 ligase and a chosen target, and the mechanism has been confirmed by ternary-complex structures, degradation kinetics and many independent groups. That is the maturity test I weigh most, and it is met at the molecular level. Biologists also received a new tool, acute and reversible post-translational knockdown, which complements genetic methods in my own field of genome maintenance. Handa's identification of cereblon explains the glue strand and shows the principle was already operating in an approved drug class (thalidomide analogues), which answers part of the chair's question about evidence short of an approved degrader. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept. The citation names both PROTACs and glues so that it describes one principle, not a single tool.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC degrader is approved, so the clinical verdict is not in, and if late-stage readouts disappoint, the prize would look early. The three-name cap leaves out Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, each with a real claim, and a critic can say the citation joins two achievements, a designed bifunctional strand and a serendipitously discovered glue strand. Sequencing (B057) and C-N coupling (B038) are fully mature and would not carry this timing risk.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B038 for Buchwald and Hartwig, citing the cleanest attribution, ubiquity in drug manufacture and no maturity concern, and lists B066 as his first alternative.
responses.response: I accept that attribution and maturity are stronger for B038 than for B066, and I have lowered my confidence in the timing of B066 slightly for that reason. But I remain unconvinced that C-N coupling is a new capability in the sense the prize requires: the 2010 prize honoured Pd-catalysed bond formation through oxidative addition, transmetalation and reductive elimination, and C-N coupling is a major extension of that mechanism by ligand design. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work reinforces the view that the concept already existed. Since you list B066 as your alternative, I would ask whether you could vote for it if B038 cannot reach five.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers B057 for Balasubramanian and Klenerman as mature, chemical and overdue, and in round 1 proposed Ciulli in place of Handa for B066.
responses.response: I agree B057 is mature and it remains my first alternative; my reservation is only whether the committee will regard the platform as chemistry and whether two names suffice, given Rothberg, Mayer and Ju. On the Ciulli question, I have reconsidered. Ciulli's VHL ligands and structures made PROTACs drug-like, but that is an optimisation of a concept already demonstrated by Crews and Deshaies, while Handa's cereblon work is an independent mechanistic discovery that explains an entire drug class. I keep Handa and record Ciulli as the strongest omitted name.

responses.point: The chair moved to B066 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa and asked whether a two-part prize, for example B066 with B022 or B057, would be stronger than a single-topic prize.
responses.response: I considered a two-part prize and decline it. With the three-person cap, any second part would force a split such as two names on degradation and one on sequencing, which weakens both parts and would leave Ciulli and Balasubramanian-Klenerman arguments unmet. A single, coherent B066 citation that covers PROTACs and glues is the more defensible public position. I share your concern that Handa anchors the glue strand, which is why the citation names both strands explicitly.

responses.point: Aili supports B066 for Crews, Deshaies and Handa, stressing the shift from occupancy-driven to event-driven pharmacology, and concedes that Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim are left out.
responses.response: I agree with the framing, and I would add the evidence short of approval that the chair requested: ternary-complex structures, thalidomide-class glues already in medical use, and independent reproduction of degradation across many targets. I differ in that I would not rest the case on pharmacology alone, since the research-tool value for biologists is also a chemical consequence of the principle. The question we still share is the risk that disappointing late-stage trials would date the prize.

responses.point: Zou prefers B038 and notes that a method rather than a new concept may struggle to reach five votes, while naming B066 as a first alternative.
responses.response: I share your view that breadth of support matters and that B038 is a method that could split the votes of B066 supporters. If the final ballot shows B066 short of five, I would find B038 an acceptable second choice for scientific reasons, though it remains behind B066 in novelty. I would not move to it first.

uncertainties: Whether members will accept recognition before the first approved degrader, or treat the lack of approval as decisive.
Whether Handa, Ciulli or Ito is the best third name, and whether a citation naming both PROTACs and glues reads as one principle.
Whether sequencing (B057) is judged chemistry and whether a third name is needed for it.
Whether the 2010 cross-coupling prize leaves room for B038.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict requires recusal. My dNTP and ribonucleotide-incorporation work is topically related to the nucleic-acid chemistry of sequencing (B057) and base editing (B022), but I have no collaboration or institutional tie to any shortlisted candidate. Nothing in the first-round exchange changes this disclosure.
